Keep the best method’s gradient unchanged and test temperature-driven selectivity to separate its critical pair. The higher temperature should also keep the last peak below 10 minutes without the low-organic hold limitation of injection 8.

Raise temperature another 10 °C while holding the gradient fixed to move beyond the central co-elution seen at 45 °C. The 55 °C scouting run suggests improved separation in this cluster, and this steeper gradient should keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Injection 10 reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark and shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. This controlled change tests whether the two pairs just above R = 1.5 retain adequate separation.

Narrow the gradient window to restore a slightly shallower slope than injection 10 while retaining the shorter programmed gradient. This tests whether trimming unused low-organic time preserves full resolution and advances the last peak; injection 10 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Lowering the starting organic fraction should help the critical central pair, whose resolution deteriorated when phi0 increased, while the narrower window makes the slope shallower than injection 11. Test whether this restores full resolution with the last peak still earlier than the maximum-score benchmark.

The maximum CRF is secured, so test a substantially faster method in a different selectivity regime. Higher temperature and a steeper gradient may carry the critical central pair through its elution-order crossover and restore separation on the other side.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 14’s slope to test initial-organic selectivity on the apparent post-crossover central pair. This should shorten retention further; monitor both the critical pair and early-peak resolution while retaining the established CRF 1.000 methods.

Test a steeper gradient to increase separation of the apparent post-crossover pair, while lowering phi0 to counter the neighboring pair’s loss of resolution seen in injection 15. This explores a faster fully resolved method while preserving injections 10 and 13 as maximum-score benchmarks.

The faster 60 °C trials trade one central overlap for another, so test a lower-temperature selectivity regime using the same gradient as injection 11. This isolates temperature effects and should keep the last peak below 10 minutes, while the two maximum-score methods remain available.

Test the unmeasured temperature between injections 3 and 9, where one central gap opens while a neighboring gap closes. Keeping their gradient fixed will reveal whether 40 °C balances those separations while retaining a last-peak time below 10 minutes.

Lengthen injection 18’s gradient by one step to test whether its sole unresolved pair responds to a shallower slope. The last peak should remain near 10 minutes, potentially yielding another fully resolved method while retaining the established maximum-score benchmarks.

Refine the successful 55 °C method with a slightly shallower gradient to increase the narrow resolution margin of its critical pair. The last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes, testing a potentially more robust maximum-score method.

Lengthen injection 12’s gradient by one step to recover its slope-sensitive central separation while preserving the stronger neighboring-pair resolution. This tests a potentially better-balanced maximum-score method, with the last peak expected below 10 minutes.

Reduce phi1 by one step to make injection 21’s gradient shallower and lift its sole deficient pair above R = 1.5. The last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes, potentially providing full resolution with more balanced margins.

Use a gradient slope between those of maximum-score injections 10 and 20, but shorten the programmed gradient to eight minutes. This should preserve full resolution with the last peak near eight minutes, testing a compact alternative to the established methods.

Preserve injection 13’s starting composition and gradient slope but end the gradient after six minutes, after the closely spaced peaks have eluted. Test whether the final hold elutes the isolated last peak within 10 minutes, retaining maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Use a slope just steeper than injection 22’s to slightly advance the last peak while aiming to preserve its balanced resolution margins. The maximum CRF is already secured; this final refinement targets another fully resolved method below 10 minutes.
